name: Alexander Schperberg

papers.title: PRISM: Bridging Multimodality and Real-Time Control in Multisensory Policies
papers.abstract: Robotic imitation learning requires policies that capture multimodal action distributions, run at real-time control rates, and effectively exploit available sensors. Existing generative approaches, including diffusion, flow matching, and IMLE, satisfy these requirements only partially. We present PRISM, a single-pass multisensory policy built on a calibrated batch-global RS-IMLE objective. We show that the RS-IMLE rejection mechanism, originally designed for few-shot image synthesis, degenerates at policy-scale batch sizes, and introduce the calibration needed to restore effective rejection. PRISM couples a temporal multisensory encoder for RGB, depth, tactile, audio, and proprioceptive inputs with a linear-attention Performer generator trained under this objective. On real-world loco-manipulation with a Unitree Go2 and 7-DoF arm, and tabletop manipulation with a UR5, PRISM improves success over diffusion policies by 10–25 percentage points while sustaining 30–50 Hz closed-loop control. On language-conditioned CALVIN ABCD, PRISM improves success by approximately 31 percentage points over diffusion and approximately 24 percentage points over flow matching, while reducing trajectory jerk by 20×–70×. Project page with videos: https://anonymous227111-png.github.io/
